rv.q: The show is both intimate and a total blast, recalling for me the glory days of older pieces like “Stomp” and “Bring in ‘Da Noise, Bring in ‘Da Funk”...
And it’s hands down the most charming, innovative and warmly embracing new musical I’ve seen in the last year.
The collective use of sounds and music as the narrative engine is especially masterful.
If this show has one major flaw, it’s that the presentation of its themes comes off a bit didactic.
Mexodus gives us the sound of, well, music, embracing the revolutionary hip-hop legacy of Hamilton and taking it, joyously, one step further.
The performers’ energy is so infectious, I can’t be the only audience member who left wishing they were hosting an afterparty.
Mexodus is an electrifying experience that explores a hidden chapter of the Underground Railroad – one that moved south, by crossing the Rio Grande toward liberation in Mexico.

cn.t: Critics hail this live-looping hip-hop two-hander as an extraordinary, knockout theatrical experience. Quijada and Robinson's dynamic performances and genre-blending beats deliver both technical brilliance and a vital human rights story.
